fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly treated as a single-phase FCC HEA, whereas the target is as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
The governing intervention is misidentified as high-stress loading rather than controlled intermediate-temperature aging, especially at approximately 600°C and 750°C.

The proposed stress-induced segregation and brittle-phase nucleation mechanism does not match the target mechanism of enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
The hypothesis omits the central non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response and the defined 550-750°C embrittlement window.
None of the cited evidence establishes stress-induced compositional segregation or brittle-phase nucleation under mechanical loading in the proposed HEA.
explanation: The response addresses the broad question of toughness loss and provides a nominally falsifiable loaded-versus-untreated comparison, but it does not reconstruct the target material, treatment, temperature boundaries, structural mediators, or non-monotonic outcome. Its experiment could test its own proposed segregation mechanism using in situ microscopy and mechanical measurements, although loading and thermal preconditioning are underspecified and confounded. The evidence is not valid support for the central claim: E1 reports cleavage in an SPS-processed alloy without stress-induced segregation; E2 concerns medium-entropy oxide ceramics; E3 supports only the general role of intrinsic plasticity in toughness; and E4 discusses deformation-induced FCC/HCP transformation rather than segregation. A discriminating target experiment would compare as-cast, 600°C-aged, and 750°C-aged AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and correlate ductility with L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC boundaries, dislocation pile-ups, and crack initiation at boundary tips while excluding grain-boundary impurity segregation.
